AuditEventOut.description:
One append-only trail entry.

Two timestamps, deliberately. ``occurred_at`` is what the reporting client
claimed; ``recorded_at`` is when the server accepted it. Keeping both means
clock skew - or a deliberately altered client clock - is visible in the
data instead of silently corrupting the ordering of the timeline.
AuditEventOut.title: AuditEventOut

AuditEventType.description:
Append-only event vocabulary.

Deliberately includes the invigilation signals the lab client will report
once it exists. ``FOCUS_LOST`` is recorded as evidence and contributes to a
warning count; it is never treated as proof of anything on its own.
AuditEventType.title: AuditEventType

CheckInRequest.description:
Sent by the candidate's client on entering the waiting room.

The machine identifier is reported by the lab client, not typed by the
candidate - binding a student to a workstation is the client's job.
CheckInRequest.title: CheckInRequest

ClientFrame.description: Base envelope for lab-client to server frames.
ClientFrame.title: ClientFrame

ComputerOut.description:
A workstation.

Deliberately has no ``student_id``. Seating is a fact about a candidate
sitting a particular exam, recorded on the session - a lab hosts a
different cohort every hour, so a permanent binding cannot hold.
ComputerOut.title: ComputerOut

ConnectionState.description:
Derived liveness, never stored.

Computed from ``now - last_heartbeat_at`` against two thresholds, so it is
always current rather than as-of the last write.
ConnectionState.title: ConnectionState

ErrorDetail.description:
Uniform error body.

``code`` is stable and machine-readable; ``message`` is for humans and may
change. Transition failures carry the states involved so the client can say
something useful rather than 'something went wrong'.
ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

ExamConfig.description:
Delivery rules applied per candidate session.

``questions_per_student`` is why the question bank exists: drawing a subset
requires a pool larger than the paper. Zero means "use the whole paper".

Randomization is materialized into the session at check-in and persisted -
never recomputed per request, or a reconnect would reshuffle the paper and
every saved answer would point at the wrong question.
ExamConfig.title: ExamConfig

ExamDetail.description:
Faculty-facing detail. Carries the answer key - never returned to a
STUDENT subject.
ExamDetail.title: ExamDetail

ExamEndingFrame.description:
Sent when the deadline is reached and the sweep begins.

Candidate writes are already refused by this point; the frame exists so the
UI can say so rather than failing a save silently.
ExamEndingFrame.title: ExamEndingFrame

ExamStartRequest.description:
Start is idempotent, so a retried request must not shift the window.

``idempotency_key`` lets the server recognise a retry of the *same* attempt
rather than a deliberate restart.
ExamStartRequest.title: ExamStartRequest

ExamStatus.description:
Exam lifecycle.

``READY`` exists because seating the roster is a real transition with
observable consequences - faculty review candidate readiness in that state,
before anyone is released into the paper.

``ENDING`` is the deadline sweep window: the clock has run out and the
server is auto-submitting stragglers, but the exam is not yet closed.
Candidate writes are refused from the moment this state is entered.
ExamStatus.title: ExamStatus

ExamSummary.description:
List-row shape. Deliberately excludes questions - an assessments table
of 200 exams must not carry every paper with it.
ExamSummary.title: ExamSummary

ExamUpdate.description: Accepted only while the exam is DRAFT. Every field optional.
ExamUpdate.title: ExamUpdate

ExamWindow.description: Returned by start. This is the authoritative exam clock.
ExamWindow.title: ExamWindow

FocusFrame.description: Focus lost or restored, reported by the lab client.
FocusFrame.title: FocusFrame

ForceSubmitFrame.description:
Instructs a candidate client to close the paper immediately.

Advisory only: the server has already stopped accepting that session's
writes. A client that ignores this frame gains nothing.
ForceSubmitFrame.title: ForceSubmitFrame

HeartbeatFrame.description: Liveness ping. High volume - held in Redis, never a row per beat.
HeartbeatFrame.title: HeartbeatFrame

HeartbeatRequest.description:
Posted by the lab client on an interval.

``occurred_at`` is what the client believes; the server records its own
arrival time separately, so a skewed or manipulated client clock is visible
in the data rather than trusted.
HeartbeatRequest.title: HeartbeatRequest

MachineEnrolRequest.description:
One-time enrolment, performed once per workstation by an administrator.

A workstation is not a user: it cannot own an exam, sit in a roster, or
reset a password. Modelling it as a user row would mean every query
touching users has to remember to exclude machines.
MachineEnrolRequest.title: MachineEnrolRequest

MonitorSummary.description:
Server-computed aggregates.

Computed server-side rather than reduced in the browser because the monitor
must stay correct when a lab has 200 sessions and the client is only
holding a page of them.
MonitorSummary.title: MonitorSummary

OptionOut.description: Faculty-facing option. Carries the answer key.
OptionOut.title: OptionOut

Principal.description:
Whoever is making the current request.

``subject_type`` is what lets one dependency guard both humans and
machines: heartbeat and event endpoints accept a machine subject, and
nothing else does.
Principal.title: Principal

QuestionOut.description:
Faculty-facing question. Carries the answer key.

Returned by ``GET /exams/{id}`` and the question-bank endpoints, all of
which require an ADMIN or FACULTY subject.
QuestionOut.title: QuestionOut

RealtimeEvent.description: WebSocket frame types. Server-sent unless noted.
RealtimeEvent.title: RealtimeEvent

ResultRow.description:
One ranked result.

``score`` is null while results are unpublished. The frontend's
``mockResultMode`` switch was standing in for exactly this: grading and
publication are separate events, and a score exists before a candidate is
allowed to see it.
ResultRow.title: ResultRow

published.description: False means scores are withheld; rows omit score and percentage.
published.title: Published

Role.description:
Who a human principal is. Machines are not users - a lab workstation
authenticates with its own credential and carries ``subject_type=machine``,
so it never appears in a roster or owns an exam.
Role.title: Role

accepted.description: False when a newer write already won; the client should refetch state.
accepted.title: Accepted

ServerFrame.description: Base envelope for everything the server pushes.
ServerFrame.title: ServerFrame

SessionDetail.description: Drill-down for one candidate, including their event timeline.
SessionDetail.title: SessionDetail

SessionEventRequest.description:
Invigilation signal reported by the lab client.

A focus loss is recorded as evidence and raises a warning count. It is never
treated, on its own, as proof of misconduct - faculty decide what a pattern
means.
SessionEventRequest.title: SessionEventRequest

SessionPaper.description:
Everything the candidate's exam screen needs, and nothing more.

Questions are :class:`StudentQuestionOut`, which has no answer-key field at
all. Ordering is this candidate's persisted shuffle.
SessionPaper.title: SessionPaper

SessionRow.description:
One row of the live monitor and of the pre-start readiness roster.

Note the two independent axes: ``status`` is lifecycle, ``connection`` is
liveness derived from ``last_heartbeat_at``. A row reading
``ACTIVE`` + ``offline`` is meaningful and common - it is a candidate who
was answering when their machine dropped.
SessionRow.title: SessionRow

SessionState.description:
Reconnect recovery payload.

After a network drop the client asks for this and reconciles: it holds the
server's view of every saved answer, so a client that missed acknowledgements
can tell what actually landed.
SessionState.title: SessionState

SessionStateFrame.description: Sent to the monitor whenever a candidate's row changes.

summary.description: Recomputed aggregates, so the monitor never re-reduces the full roster.

SessionStateFrame.title: SessionStateFrame

SessionStatus.description:
Per-candidate lifecycle.

Note what is absent: there is no ``DISCONNECTED`` member. Liveness is a
separate axis (:class:`ConnectionState`) derived from the heartbeat, so a
candidate can be correctly described as "ACTIVE but offline for 40s".
Folding the two together would lose what the candidate was doing when the
network dropped, which is exactly what an invigilator needs to know.
SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus

option.description: Index into the options as ordered for this candidate.
option.title: Option

StudentOptionOut.description:
Candidate-facing option.

No ``is_correct``. The field does not exist on this model, so no serializer
setting, response_model override, or future refactor can leak it.

``position`` is this candidate's shuffled position, not the authored one.
StudentOptionOut.title: StudentOptionOut

StudentQuestionOut.description:
Candidate-facing question.

Ordering reflects the per-session shuffle materialized at check-in, so the
paper is stable across reconnects. Marks are shown because candidates are
told what each question is worth; nothing here reveals the answer.

position.description: Position in this candidate's paper, not the authored order.
position.title: Position

StudentQuestionOut.title: StudentQuestionOut

SubjectType.description: What kind of principal a token represents.
SubjectType.title: SubjectType

SubmissionReceipt.description: Returned by submit, and re-returned verbatim on a repeat submit.
SubmissionReceipt.title: SubmissionReceipt

WarningFrame.description:
An invigilation signal worth surfacing.

Evidence for a human to judge, not an accusation the system makes.
WarningFrame.title: WarningFrame

info.description: Phase 2 contract. Handlers return static examples; the shapes, status codes and operation ids are final and generate the frontend client.
info.summary: Server-authoritative examination platform for physical computer labs.
info.title: Exam Control API

get.description: Append-only trail. There is deliberately no delete endpoint.

post.description:
Human sign-in. The response carries ``server_time`` so the client can
establish its clock offset before anything is timed.

One-time workstation enrolment, performed by an administrator.

Returns the machine secret exactly once; it is stored hashed.

Exchanges a machine credential for a short-lived token carrying
``subject_type=machine``. Such a token may only reach heartbeat and event
endpoints.

Liveness ping from a workstation. Machine subjects only.

High volume by design - 60 machines in a lab. Held in Redis rather than
written as a row per beat.

get.description: Backs the assessments table and the dashboard.

post.description: Creates the exam as a DRAFT.

get.description:
Faculty-facing detail, including answer keys.

Never reachable by a STUDENT subject; candidates read their paper through
``GET /sessions/{id}`` instead.

patch.description: Rejected with 409 unless the exam is still DRAFT.

409.description: The exam is not in a state that permits this transition.

post.description: Requires a reason, which is written to the audit trail as CRITICAL.

409.description: The exam is not in a state that permits this transition.

post.description: Closes the exam early. Enters ENDING and begins the sweep.

409.description: The exam is not in a state that permits this transition.

get.description:
Server-computed aggregates plus rows.

Also the documented fallback when the websocket is unavailable: the same
reducer consumes this and a live frame, so losing the socket degrades the
refresh rate rather than correctness.
Ranked results. Scores are omitted while unpublished.

post.description: Releases scores to candidates by setting ``published_at``.

DRAFT to SCHEDULED, then seats the roster to reach READY.

Validates the roster against lab capacity inside the same transaction. The
frontend performs this check too, but only as UX - a candidate can edit the
client, so this is where it actually holds.

409.description: The exam is not in a state that permits this transition.

get.description: The readiness roster before start, and the monitor table during.

post.description:
Stamps the authoritative window and releases waiting candidates.

Idempotent: a retry with the same idempotency key returns the existing
window rather than shifting it, and candidates already answering are left
untouched.

409.description: The exam is not in a state that permits this transition.

get.description:
Workstations and their derived liveness.

No candidate is attached here: seating belongs to the session, because a
lab hosts a different cohort every hour.
Assessments the authenticated candidate is enrolled in.
The paper as ordered for this candidate. Carries no answer keys.

put.description:
Idempotent upsert of one answer.

``client_seq`` lets a stale write that arrives late after a reconnect be
discarded without relying on either clock.

409.description: The exam is not LIVE or the session is not ACTIVE, so writes are refused.

post.description:
Enters the waiting room and materializes this candidate's paper.

The question and option ordering is drawn **once, here**, and persisted on
the session. Recomputing it per request would reshuffle the paper on
reconnect and leave every saved answer pointing at the wrong question.

get.description:
Invigilator drill-down: identity, machine, timings, and event timeline.

Faculty scope - this is the monitor's detail drawer, not a candidate view.

post.description:
Invigilation signal from the lab client. Machine subjects only.

Accepted and recorded as evidence; a focus loss raises a warning count but
is never treated on its own as proof of misconduct.

put.description: Toggles the review flag for one question.

409.description: The exam is not LIVE or the session is not ACTIVE, so writes are refused.

get.description:
Reconnect recovery.

Returns the server's view of every saved answer, so a client that missed
acknowledgements during a network drop can tell what actually landed
instead of guessing.

post.description:
Final submission.

Idempotent: a repeat call returns the original receipt rather than
recording a second submission.

409.description: The exam is not LIVE or the session is not ACTIVE, so writes are refused.
